lines.text: Nineteen seventy-three, over Abidjan. A passenger plane hits a vulture.
Altitude: eleven thousand three hundred metres.
The plane landed safely. And no bird has been recorded higher.
Now flip that upside down. The deepest point in the ocean, Challenger Deep, is ten thousand nine hundred and thirty-five metres down.
So that vulture was three hundred and sixty-five metres higher than the ocean is deep.
And it wasn't anywhere near the top of the sky.
So what's flying above that, and how far up does it go? It starts at level four, and the full video is linked right here.
